intent: Hold the best-measured geometry (iteration 1, 4 and 6 reference): five 12 mm sensors at y = 0.05 m spanning ±0.03 m at 15 mm spacing, with the wheel, body and mass values unchanged. Expected result: a score near 69.3 and line_loss_events about 1 per run, which would confirm the reference is reproducible. I am not changing any geometry this iteration because every single-variable change tested so far has lowered the score. Under consideration without committing: a wider 5-sensor span of ±0.05 m at y = 0.05 m, but only if line loss falls clearly below 1 per run, which the ±0.04 m result does not suggest. A controller-side fix for line-loss handling is the more likely lever, and that belongs to the Integrator.
learning: Span results at 12 mm and y = 0.05 m: ±0.024 m scored 54.37 (with a controller change), ±0.03 m scored 69.32, and ±0.04 m scored 52.47, so ±0.03 m is the best measured span. The 16 mm footprint and y = 0.03 m both lowered the score. Line loss has stayed near 1 per run under every geometry, so the next lever is most likely the controller's line-loss handling. If this iteration does not reproduce about 69, the difference is the controller and the geometry should stay as it is.
rationale: The evidence is consistent across iterations 0 to 6. The best-measured geometry is the iteration 1 design: five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 m, with y = 0.05 m, on a 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.6 kg mass and a 0.16 x 0.14 m body. It scored 69.3241 in iterations 1, 4 and 6, so the result reproduces with the same controller. Each change away from it lowered the score: the 16 mm footprint (54.45, iteration 2), y = 0.03 m (59.64, iteration 3) and the span of ±0.04 m (52.47, iteration 5). Line loss stayed near 1 per run in every iteration (1.0 to 1.65), and it did not fall clearly below 1 per run with any geometry tested, so the sensor layout has only partly reduced it. Steering oscillation (0.07 to 0.15) is not the limiting factor. The Integrator's feedback advises holding this geometry and does not ask for a new variable, so I am taking that advice. Iteration 2 is confounded by a controller change, but iteration 3 was not, and the reversion in iteration 4 confirmed that y = 0.05 m is the better offset. Wheel track, wheel radius, mass and body have no evidence pointing at them, and body width does not move the off-track limit: max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) = 0.06 m across the allowed range. I considered a wider span (±0.05 m) but the ±0.04 m result gives no support for it, so I am not committing to that test now. Expected result: a score near 69.3, with line_loss_events about 1 per run.
